reviews.review:
I basically bought this game because TotalBiscuit loved it so many years ago. It starts off amazing. The combat looks and feels impactful and the game really does make an effort to make you feel like a respected Angel of Death, in an out of combat. You crash through hordes of Orks in combat, and friendly soldiers salute and whisper excitedly as you pass them by. 

But the game is not without fault, and the more you play the more of them you find. The weapons are somewhat interesting, but all of them have some great flaw or another, pressumably to prevent the player from just using the same thing till the end or keeping the illusion of side-grades going, as you continue to find ammo refill stations with weapons lying around allowing you to switch them on the go. But really there's clear "best" guns: in close quarters the shotgun is the best--but you can only carry 10 ammo for it--and at long range the Lascannon is best--but again only 15 ammo. The standard pistol (and later plasma pistol) and bolter (and later Kraken bolter) feel quite mediocre at best by the end of the game, but you are forced to keep them. Even when you get access to a plasma rifle that seems to be a natural replacement to the Kraken Bolter, the game doesn't allow you to make that replacement, instead you have to give up one of your other two weapons and keep the krappy Kraken. Pressumably because the developers were worried you'd run out of ammo on all your weapons, despite the ammo boxes lying every 15 feet.

The weapon system has further frustrations. The melee weapons are something of a disappointment: the axe is a marginal upgrade to the chainsword but it seems better in every functional way, but the sword is imo cooler and more satisfying to use due to the sound effects. The hammer is marginally better in damage, but forces you to only use the pistol or bolter, so essentially you have to pick between using the best melee weapon or the best ranged weapons. This is a horrible choice to force onto the player, because melee weapons are really a sort of threshhold as to which enemies you are allowed to finish off for health, with stronger enemies requiring a higher "tier" of weapon otherwise they just bash your face in if you try to use a finisher on them. This is made even worse by the fact that those finishers are your main way to recover health, and late game enemies melt through your health like butter even on Normal difficulty. Thus if you try to melee them your health disappears, and in order to get your health back you have to use melee finishers which require you to carry the hammer and not be able to use the best ranged weapons. Amazing really.

Speaking of the finishers. They can go right to hell. At the start of the game they feel awesome. Then you do them a dozen times and realize there's only about 3 basic animations for them. Each new melee weapon maybe adds one more. And then you realize these animations seem to take a long time. A lot longer than they need to. And then you realize they don't prevent you from taking damage. And that you only recover the health at the end of the overly long animation for most of them. And then you die a handful of times because you're performing an overly long animation and get shot in the process, or maybe one of those suicde bombers spawns in and blows you up while you're locked in. All great fun. 

You are quickly given new weapons, but many of them are only marginal improvements to the previous lot, and some are downright disappointments. Examples of these imo include the Hammer which prevents you from using the more powerful and more enjoyable ranged weapons, the storm bolter which again fails to replace the basic Kraken and is useless beyond point blank range. Hell basically anything other than the meltagun and lascannon can go on that list. 

The game became an exercise in frustration towards the end of the game. I've never before been so empathically hoping for a game to finish already. Only reasons I finished it was I had come this far and TB had loved it so much, I was hoping something would redeem it. But no, I just slugged my way through to the end. And then the final boss battle was a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ quick time event chain. 

Despite all my frustrations with the game, there is some enjoyment to be had here. So perhaps it's worth your time if you get it on a good discount. The highlights are probably the Jetpack sections, which number about three in the game and are fairly brief likely due to their simplicity and thus not wanting to overstay their welcome. The game is of course quite old so multiplayer is difficult to come by, but it seems some groups still play it. I managed to find one Exterminatus match--apparently a sort of Co-Op PVP horde mode vs Orks--and evidently you start off with a horrible loadout (basic bolter and knife with a couple grenades) and can only unlock the Customizer if you reach level 4. Welp, seems that's not happening--at least not for me.

All in all, I can only recommend it at a discount--and just barely at that. Probably better if you're a 40K fan, though I thought some aspects were cool even with very limited exposure to the series.

Such a fun, simple, FPS. Amazing if you're already into 40k.
Shame no one's playing
